$comment: Root Deno 2.x workspace. Members are added here as each package is scaffolded. Path aliases per documentation/architecture/SYSTEM_ARCHITECTURE.md §2. Do NOT list a member directory that does not yet exist — Deno errors on missing members.
$comment:media: @jsquash/{jpeg,png,webp} + omggif are the server-side media pipeline (packages/backend/services/media): the Squoosh codecs (mozjpeg, libpng, libwebp) compiled to WASM decode and encode, and omggif (pure JS) reads a GIF's first frame. All WASM/JS, so they run with read permission alone and unchanged under `deno serve`, Deno Deploy and Supabase Edge Functions. Two alternatives were tried and rejected: native `sharp` does not load under Deno's npm resolution, and `imagescript`'s npm build loads a platform-specific `.node` binary at import time (needs --allow-ffi). Licences: Apache-2.0 (@jsquash/*), MIT (omggif). Loaded ONLY inside the pipeline Worker, never into the Vite SSR bundle.
$comment:inspector: three (+ @types/three, which Deno pairs with `three` only because it is mapped here and installed), pdfjs-dist (the LEGACY build — the modern build calls Map.prototype.getOrInsertComputed / Math.sumPrecise natively), highlight.js core + per-language modules, dompurify for marked output, docx-preview for .docx pages. Client-only: dynamically imported inside the file inspector's island effects through memoised loaders (apps/web/features/inspector/core/*-loader.ts), never at module scope — Fresh's server snapshot evaluates every island module. Engines only: never import their CSS; every surface is reskinned with tokens. pdf.js wasm/cmaps/fonts/iccs and the three Draco/Basis decoders are served at /vendor/* by the vendorAssets() plugin in vite.config.ts, never committed. Versions are exact pins (newest release at least 14 days old when added). Licences: MIT (three, @types/three), Apache-2.0 (pdfjs-dist, docx-preview), BSD-3-Clause (highlight.js), MPL-2.0 OR Apache-2.0 (dompurify), MIT OR GPL-3.0 (jszip, docx-preview's dependency, used under MIT).

tasks.$comment:dev: Two dev modes, one flag. `dev` pins USE_MOCKS=false so the name is a guarantee rather than a hope — it serves whatever each *_BACKEND_LIVE gate in .env allows, which is the database. `dev:mock` pins it true, which overrides every gate at once and serves fixtures. The prefix wins over .env because apps/web/main.ts calls dotenv load({export:true}), and that never overwrites a variable the process already has (verified, not assumed). Deno task shell supports POSIX env prefixes on Windows too, so this needs no cross-env dependency. The port is NOT pinned here: vite.config.ts reads `PORT` from the shell, then the untracked `.env.local`, then `.env`, defaulting to 3000 with strictPort, so a machine where 3000 is taken sets `PORT=4000` in `.env.local` and changes nothing for anyone else. A `--port` flag still overrides it.
tasks.$comment:build: One pass builds everything. The workspace members (packages/types, packages/ui, packages/backend) have NO separate compile step — they are consumed as TypeScript source through the import map, so Vite type-strips and bundles them alongside the app. `vite build` drives both Fresh environments: the client environment emits the island bundles into _fresh/client, the ssr environment emits the route chunks + _fresh/server.js. There is nothing to build before it and nothing to build after it.
tasks.$comment:serve: Runs an EXISTING production build. `_fresh/server.js` is written by @fresh/plugin-vite and default-exports { fetch }, which is exactly the shape `deno serve` expects. `--unstable-kv` is not required — the shared handle (packages/backend/core/kv.ts) feature-detects `Deno.openKv` and FxService and the query-vector cache (EmbeddingBackendService) fall back to per-isolate memory caches — but without it the 15-minute FX rate cache and the 7-day query-vector cache are lost on every isolate, so each cold isolate re-embeds popular searches.
tasks.$comment:start: Build, then start the production SSR server. This is the single self-contained entry point: `deno task start`.
tasks.start: deno task build && deno task serve
tasks.$comment:budget:landing: The landing pages' JavaScript budget (documentation/flows/LANDING.md §7, Decision #286 (A): landing-owned initial JS ≤ 60 kB gzip, the app baseline held at its measured size, pinned in bytes, the hero island ≤ 20 kB, each landing lazy chunk ≤ 35 kB; layout hosts, footer and signed-in totals reported) measured on the PRODUCTION build: it reads apps/web/_fresh/client/.vite/manifest.json, takes the client entry plus every island the page renders (declared in apps/web/features/landing/core/js-budget.ts, checked against the source by island-graph.test.ts) and their static imports, gzips each chunk once, and prints a table. Exits 1 over budget, 2 without a usable build. Run `deno task build` first (`deno task build && deno task budget:landing`). No server is started.
tasks.$comment:db: `db:reset` rebuilds the local database from the consolidated migrations, runs supabase/seeds/*.sql (18 personas incl. the platform operator / 3 teams / 2 businesses / 7 projects / wallets / messages), then uploads supabase/seed-assets/** into the storage buckets declared in config.toml. `--yes` answers the CLI's per-bucket "already exists, overwrite properties?" prompt, which it asks because the bucket rows are owned by migration 00005040 — plain `supabase db reset` works too and only needs Enter at each prompt. `db:seed:generate` regenerates the committed seed SQL + asset tree from the mock corpus and supabase/seeds/gen/world.ts; run it after editing either, then commit the output.
tasks.$comment:db:editorial: Editorial content (the help centre, the changelog, Projective's articles — Decision #274) is platform reference data that must exist in every environment, so it is NOT the development seed: `db:editorial:generate` emits each surface's Zod-validated content source (packages/backend/services/editorial/content/<surface>.ts) into ONE category-5 migration per surface (supabase/migrations/0000507x_seed_editorial_*.sql). Commit the output with the source; `--check` exits 1 while any file is stale, and content-sql.test.ts fails the unit gate the same way.
tasks.$comment:check: Entry points, not `deno check .`: the latter walks build output and any stray git worktree under .claude/, which is not this repo's code. The routes globs are NOT redundant with `apps/web/main.ts`: routes are discovered from the filesystem at runtime and are in NO module's import graph, so before they were listed here `deno task check` type-checked not one of the ~200 route files — a whole class of error (a route calling a fat-service method that does not exist, a handler returning the wrong shape) passed the merge gate silently. Verified by measurement: with the graph-only form, `deno check apps/web/main.ts` exits 0 while `deno check apps/web/routes/api/projects/setup.ts` reports the missing method. `**` is expanded by the task shell, on Windows too.
tasks.$comment:test: The merge gate. `--allow-env` is needed because the backend env reader is pulled in transitively by anything touching a service; `--allow-read` for module loading.
tasks.$comment:smoke:stripe: Stripe rails smoke (card escrow round trip, payout gate + transfer, reconciliation) against the local Supabase stack and stripe-mock (`docker run -d -p 12111:12111 stripe/stripe-mock`); the ledger half runs in a rolled-back transaction. Not part of `test` because it needs Docker. SYSTEM_ARCHITECTURE §Stripe 1.3.
tasks.$comment:embeddings: Stores a voyage-4 vector for every PUBLIC discovery item (Decision #179): reads the catalogue as anon, skips items whose stored text hash and model still match, embeds the rest in batches and writes them through search.fn_set_embedding with SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY. Needs VOYAGE_API_KEY in .env.local. db:reset leaves every vector empty, so run this after it. --dry-run prints the entity count, a token estimate and the cost estimate without calling Voyage or writing; --force re-embeds unchanged items too. Independent of EMBEDDINGS_ENABLED, which only decides whether discovery reads the vectors.
tasks.$comment:cron: Runs one job from the registry (ops.scheduled_jobs, Decision #203) now: `deno task cron:run <job>`, or `--list` for every job and its cadence. A sql job runs in the database through ops.run_job with SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY; an http job POSTs to APP_URL + its path with the bearer from .env.local, exactly as pg_cron + pg_net send it, so the app must be running. pg_cron runs the same jobs on their schedules; this is the by-hand path.
tasks.$comment:test:e2e: Browser smoke against a RUNNING dev server and the local Supabase stack (Playwright via npm:playwright-core, Chromium from E2E_CHROMIUM, /opt/pw-browsers/chromium, the Playwright cache or installed Chrome). Not part of `test` because it needs both. The catalogue suite expects the `web-catalogue-e2e` launch config (port 13217, CATALOGUE_BACKEND_LIVE=false so Analytics/Clients answer fixtures); see the header of apps/web/tests/e2e/catalogue.spec.ts. The contact suite expects the `web-contact-e2e` launch config (port 13330, CONTACT_BACKEND_LIVE=false, so nothing is stored); see the header of apps/web/tests/e2e/contact.spec.ts.
tasks.$comment:test:e2e:public: The public routes' integration smoke (Decision #279, PUBLIC_ROUTES P8): every legal, help, contact, about, changelog, articles and feedback page at 375/768/1280 px, light and dark, with reduced motion — status, console, broken assets, one h1, landmarks, JSON-LD, horizontal scroll, axe-core WCAG A/AA (a test-only npm:axe-core import, never in the import map) and a screenshot each — plus the feeds, the PDF, the sitemap and robots.txt, and a mobile layout-shift budget (CLS < 0.05) on an article and a help article. Its own task because it needs its own server: the `web-public-e2e` launch config (port 13380, the editorial, community, contact, finance and newsletter gates off, so it reads fixtures and stores nothing); see the header of apps/web/tests/e2e/public-routes.spec.ts. E2E_SHOTS names the screenshot directory.
tasks.test: deno task check && deno task lint && deno task test:unit
tasks.$comment:fmt: Deliberately NOT part of `test`, for two reasons that are facts about this repo rather than preferences. (1) `core.autocrlf=true` means a Windows checkout has CRLF in the working tree while `deno fmt` wants LF, so `--check` reports every file as unformatted there no matter what anyone commits. (2) ~280 files predate the formatter, and reformatting them wholesale would bury real diffs. Format the files you touch (`deno fmt <paths>`) rather than the tree.
